items.title: No cap on gun ownership in Tasmania after Labor amendment fails

children.content: There will not be a cap on the number of guns a person can own in Tasmania, after the lower house voted not to amend the state government's firearms reform legislation.

items.title: Authorities determine Tasmanian power station fire was accidental

children.content: The fire service confirms the blaze that gutted the Tungatinah Power Station last week began on the assembly bay floor and was accidental.

image.altText: A burnt out power station. The scaffolding remains but the walls are gone.

items.title: Full booking capacity for new Spirit ferries not yet available, ahead of first sailings

children.content: Travellers hoping to jump on the new Spirit of Tasmania ferries with their cars and caravans in the coming months may have to wait, with bookings still limited to the capacity of the current ships. But TT-Line says that's not forever.

image.altText: View of a new Spirit of Tasmania ferry passing one of the older Spirit ferries that is docked.

items.title: Rib contouring surgery raises ethical concerns in Australia

children.content: A cosmetic surgery procedure that reshapes and partially fractures the ribs is being offered in Australia after gaining popularity with influencers overseas. Experts warn social media promotion of the procedure could fuel pressure to achieve increasingly extreme body shapes.

children.content: The iPhone Duo will start at $3,499, putting it among the most expensive mainstream smartphones on the market and marking the first major test for Apple's new CEO.

children.content: Former Liberal MP Moira Deeming will contest the November election with Family First, having been cast out of her former party in July.

items.title: Officer in Dezi Freeman search given job back after on-duty drink driving

children.content: After rear-ending a vehicle in September last year, the officer blew a 0.07 breath test and told Victoria's police disciplinary board that he drank two "very strong" bourbon and cokes about three hours earlier.

items.title: Women's tennis has a new world number one as US Open showdown looms

children.content: Elena Rybakina becomes world number one for the first time by reaching the US Open semifinals, despite defending champion and current top-ranked player Aryna Sabalenka still being alive in the tournament.

image.altText: Elena Rybakina seen through her racquet strings at the US Open.
